note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prior prostate cancer diagnosis following PSA fluctuation and recent imaging findings.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. Patient is a 60-year-old male with a history of coronary artery disease, currently managed with aspirin 80 mg and atorvastatin. He works as a tram driver, married, lives with his partner, and maintains an active lifestyle with running 3x/week. Recent PSA trend shows fluctuation, with a notable decrease in Feb 2024 followed by a rise in Jan 2025. No new urological symptoms reported, but mild LUTS with IPSS score 7. Mobility limitation noted, requiring ground-floor consultation. Recent dermatology appointment for actinic keratosis check.

On DRE, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged without nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical T stage cT1c. General examination reveals stable vital signs, BP 106/75 mmHg, HR 66 bpm. No signs of metastatic disease or acute urological complications.
